body:
119 BENEFIT DELIVERY TIME FRAMES (AAM)

SR 15-26 Dated 07/15 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

As long as all State Supplement Program (SSP) eligibility requirements are met at the time the first SSP benefit allotment is issued, SSP financial assistance, which includes the Aid to the Permanently and Totally Disabled (APTD), Old Age Assistance (OAA), and Aid to the Needy Blind (ANB) programs, begins the first day of the *semimonthly payment period in which SSP eligibility is determined. See Section 617.01 , Assistance Payments: Determination, Frequency, and Issuance , for more information.

*

Exceptions:

. When an ANB or APTD application is denied solely due to a *Disability Determination Unit (DDU) decision that an individual is not considered blind or disabled, and the DDU decision is subsequently reversed by DDU or an administrative appeal, financial assistance begins on the first day of the month of that denial decision, provided that:

- all general, technical, and categorical eligibility requirements were met during the entire month in which the original DDU denial decision was made, and

- the individual is currently eligible.

. When eligibility is based on a life insurance offset (see Life Insurance Offset in Part 411, Life Insurance Offset) , begin financial assistance on the same day as medical assistance.

. When an eligibility determination is made after the 45-day or 90-day application processing periods (see PART 116 , APPLICATION PROCESSING TIME FRAMES ), financial assistance begins effective with the payment period of the month in which:

- the 45 th day fell, for OAA and ANB applicants; or

- the 90 th day fell, for APTD applicants.

Exception : When an eligibility decision is made after the 45 or 90 days application processing period because a decision could not be reached because the applicant or an examining physician delayed or failed to take a required action, or because there was an administrative or other emergency beyond DHHS' control, cash begins the first day of the semimonthly payment period in which SSP eligibility is determined after that 45 th or 90 th day, as long as SSP eligibility requirements are met at the time the first SSP benefit allotment is issued.

References : He-W 672.02, RSA 167:10, 42 CFR 435.912(a), (c), & (e)

121 INTERVIEWS (AAM)

SR 24-31 Dated 12/24 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

A t initial application and at least every 12-month redetermination, the household must participate in either an in-person or phone interview.

Interviews are official and confidential discussions regarding an individual’s household circumstances. During the interview, the following shall occur:

• An evaluation of all available information, including any existing case record;

• Resolution of any unclear or incomplete information;

• An individual’s rights and responsibilities are provided and reviewed; and

• Individuals are provided information about program policies and procedures.

An interview will be conducted prior to each initial eligibility determination and at each subsequent redetermination.

If applicable, interview an authorized representative if the individual cannot participate in the interview because of age, incapacity, illness, transportation difficulties, employment, language barriers, or similar reasons.

Exceptions:

• Cases eligible to be redetermined via mail-in or online redetermination process are not required to participate in an in-pereson interview. However, one must be granted if it is requested. DHHS may also require an interview as a result of reported changes or the discovery of conflicting information regarding eligibility criteria. (See PART 155 , REDETERMINATION).

References : He-W 636.01; He-W 644.01; He-W 684.01; RSA 167:8; 45 CFR 206.10

SR 24-31 Dated 12/24 Previous Policy

An in-person interview is conducted at the applicant’s local district office. The place where the interview is conducted must preserve the privacy and confidentiality of the interview.

Applicants can also choose to have a phone interview instead of coming into the District Office for an in-person interview. All phone interviews must preserve the privacy and confidentiality of the interview.

All program and verification requirements remain the same whether the applicant participates in a phone or in-person interview.

SR 94-04 Dated 04/94 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

When the individual fails to appear for an interview without good cause by the 30 th day after the application for financial assistance was filed the application shall be denied.

When the individual contacts the office within 30 days of the original application filing date, BFA Form 807, Interview Appointment Notice , is provided to the individual with a new interview date and time.

Good cause exists if the reason for failure to appear was beyond the individual’s control. DHHS is solely responsible for determining good cause.

References : He-W 636.01; He-W 644.01; He-W 684.01; RSA 167:8

Editorial Revisions Made: 11/2023

135 ADVANCE NOTICE PERIOD (ANP) (AAM)

SR 03-14 Dated 02/03 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

Notify individuals in advance of termination of assistance, a decrease in the level of eligibility, or a decrease in the amount of benefits. The time frame between the date the NOD is generated and the date the action actually takes effect is called the advance notice period (ANP).

The standard ANP is 10 days. Under some circumstances the ANP is not required, is reduced to 5 days, or is expanded to 30 days. The effect of the ANP on benefits is as follows:

. Financial Assistance - Terminating cases receive only payments due prior to the expiration of the ANP. Decreasing cases receive the lower payment for the payroll in which the ANP expires.

. Medical Assistance - Terminations are effective the last day of the ANP. See Part 161 , Termination of Medical Assistance, QMB, and SLMB, for Exceptions . Decreases in level of eligibility are effective the day after the ANP expires.

body:
135.01 Administrative Appeal Requests and the ANP (AAM)

SR 13-12 Dated 9/13 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

If an individual requests an administrative appeal within *15 days from the date on the notice of the termination of APTD cash assistance , continue assistance at the pre-change level pending the appeal decision. If an individual requests an administrative appeal after the *15 days expire, or if there is no advance notice period (ANP), the termination or decrease takes effect on schedule.

Any benefits received during pending appeals is subject to recoupment if the Administrative Appeals Unit (AAU) does not find in favor of the individual.

Exception: Individuals whose APTD cash assistance was denied or terminated because the individual was denied Social Security Administration (SSA)-related benefits because the individual did not meet SSA medical criteria, can only continue to receive cash assistance at the pre-change level pending the AAU decision when the following criteria are met:

• The request for continued receipt of APTD cash assistance pending the appeal is received within 15 days from the date on the notice of the termination of APTD cash assistance; and

• Within that same 15-day period, the individual provides documentation signed and dated by a physician, physician’s assistant (PA), advanced practice registered nurse (APRN), or psychologist which in cludes the printed name of the health professional, the specialty of the health professional, and the address and phone number of the health professional, and states:

- that the individual’s medical condition has increased in severity during the 12 months prior to the date the individual requested the administrative appeal; or

- that the medical condition for which the SSA based the decision to deny the individual SSA benefits is unrelated to the medical information upon which the Disability Determination Unit (DDU) based the decision to approve the individual for APTD benefits.

Note : The statement from the physician, PA, APRN, or psychologist regarding a medical condition increasing in severity must specify the increase happened at some point within the last 12 months prior to the date the individual requested an administrative appeal. If the increasing severity of the medical condition happened over a period of time longer than 12 months, or at some point prior to 12 months, the individual cannot receive continued benefits while pending the appeal.

EXAMPLES : A physician, PA, APRN, or psychologist’s statement indicates that an individual’s medical condition has increased in severity:

• due to an incident which happened 13 months prior to the date the individual filed the administrative appeal. This individual would not be eligible for continued receipt of APTD cash benefits while the individual is waiting for the AAU decision because the incident happened more than 12 months prior to the date the individual filed the administrative appeal.

• over the course of the individual’s illness, which they have been suffering from over the past 5 years. This individual would not be eligible for continued receipt of APTD cash benefits while the individual is waiting for the AAU decision because the increase in severity happened over a period of time longer than 12 months prior to the date the individual filed the administrative appeal.

• 2 days prior to the individual’s submission of the request for an administrative appeal. This individual would be eligible for continued receipt of APTD cash benefits while the individual is waiting for the AAU decision because the incident happened less than 12 months prior to the date the individual filed the administrative appeal.

If the individual fails to provide the documentation above, or the documentation provided does not demonstrate that the requirements have been met, the individual is not eligibility for continued receipt of APTD cash assistance pending the appeal.

If the termination of APTD cash assistance is ultimately overturned at the appeals hearing:

• due to the individual’s medical condition having increased in severity during the 12 months prior to the date the individual requested the administrative appeal, provide the individual 30 days from the date the District Office receives the AAU decision to verify that the individual:

- has appealed the SSA denial; and

- has sent SSA the documentation regarding the increased severity of their medical condition.

• because the medical condition for which the SSA denied SSA benefits is not the medical condition for which the individual was approved APTD cash assistance, provide the individual 30 days from the date the District Office receives the AAU decision to verify that the individual:

- has reapplied for SSA benefits; and

- that the medical condition for which the individual has reapplied for SSA benefits is the same medical condition for which DDU approved the individual for APTD cash assistance.

If the individual fails to provide verification within 30 days, and APTD is then terminated, do not continue APTD cash assistance pending the appeal decision.

Any benefits received during pending appeals is subject to recoupment if the AAU does not find in favor of the individual.

135.03 No ANP Required (AAM)

SR 94-04 Dated 04/94 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

There is no ANP when any of the following circumstances result in termination of assistance, decreases in the level of eligibility, or decreases in the amount of benefits:

• The individual provides a written, signed request to voluntarily terminate assistance.

• The individual ’ s location is unknown, and DFA mail is returned by the Postal Service indicating no forwarding address is on file.

• The individual has been accepted for assistance in a new state.

• The individual is placed in a nursing facility or long term hospitalization.

• The individual is admitted or committed to a public institution and is no longer eligible for public assistance.

• The individual is deceased.

• The individual requests in writing to voluntarily initiate, change, or remove a vendor payee, or to change the amount of a vendor payment

• The individual has been getting a positive grant adjustment and the adjustment period is complete. Notify the individual in writing, at the start of the adjustment, of the date the adjustment period ends.

• An individual or assistance group is closed in one case and opened in another, due to administrative procedures, and the level of eligibility and amount of assistance remains the same.

155 REDETERMINATION (AAM)

SR 23-04 Dated 02/23 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

Redetermine eligibility for all individuals at regularly scheduled intervals at least every 12 months. See PART 127 , LENGTH OF ELIGIBILITY .

Review and verify all eligibility factors and criteria subject to change. Update eligibility and benefits, as necessary.

12-Month Redetermination

The following cases are redetermined via the online or mail-in redetermination process at 12-month intervals:

· Adult categories of financial, with or without SNAP, and with all financial, medical and SNAP case sizes equal;

· QMB, QDWI, SLMB, and SLMB135 with or without SNAP; and

· Nursing Facility Care.

6-Month Redetermination

Adult categories of financial assistance with SNAP, and with varied financial/medical and SNAP case sizes, are redetermined via the online or mail-in redetermination process for the first 6-month redetermination; the next redetermination is conducted via face-to-face/phone redetermination process.

Continue this alternating method of redetermination as long as the assistance group remains eligible for benefits.

References : He-W 644.01, He-W 684.01, He-W 684.02, He-W 606.92, 42 CFR 435.916

155.01 Timely Notice (AAM)

SR 23-04 Dated 02/23 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

Inform each individual of the need to review eligibility before benefits can be continued.

Notify individuals based on their household circumstances, that they are required to participate in a regularly scheduled redetermination via mail in, face-to-face/phone or online.

Face-To-Face/Phone Redetermination

A rede Interview letter , is sent to individuals who are required to participate in a face-to-face/phone redetermination and is generated by the 15 th of the month prior to the month the redetermination is due .

The letter advises the individual:

• of the date and time of the eligibility interview;

• that the individual must call to reschedule the interview if unable to attend the appointment and the individual wishes to continue receiving benefits; and

• of the effect on benefits for failure to attend;

The letter to the individual includes:

• BFA Form 775, Rental Verification Request ; and

• BFA Form 756, Employment Verification .

For a face-to-face/phone redetermination the individual must complete the BFA Form 800, Application for Assistance , or indicate any changes on the Eligibility Interview Summary (EIS) ; and participate in a face-to-face/phone interview.

Online or Mail-In Redetermination

Mail-In Redetermination

A mail-in redetermination package is sent to cases that are eligible for this type of redetermination by the 15th of the month prior to the month the redetermination is due.

The package includes:

• New HEIGHTS-generated CS0005, Mail-In Rede Letter ;

• a postage-paid business reply envelope;

• BFA Form 811R, Application: Your Rights and Responsibilities ; and

• BFA Form 800R, Application for Continued Eligibility for Financial, Medical, Child Care, and SNAP Benefits .

The letter advises the individual :

• of verifications needed to process the case;

• of the due date of the verification - 15th day of the last month of the redetermination period; and

• to contact the District Office if they have any questions.

Online Redetermination

Recipients with NH EASY accounts who are scheduled for what would usually be considered a mail-in redetermination are also eligible to complete their redetermination online.

If the NH EASY account holder ’ s redetermination method is "online", the online redetermination letter is generated by the 15th of the month prior to the month the redetermination is due.

The letter advises the individual:

• that household must complete the online Redetermination Application and send in all needed verifications by the 15th day of the following month;

• if the household does not complete the online redetermination process and/or provide all needed verifications by the due date, it will result in a termination of benefits;

• that the household may opt out of the online redetermination process and return to a mail-in redetermination process; and

• the household should contact the District Office if they have any questions.

The letter to the individual will also include:

• a postage-paid business reply Central Scanning Unit (CSU) envelope for the recipient to provide their verifications.

Individuals eligible to participate in the online or mail-in redetermination process are not required to participate in a face-to-face/phone interview. However, an interview must be granted if one is requested.

Exception: Require a face-to-face/phone interview for individuals who do not fully complete BFA Form 800R or do not complete the online Redetermination Application.

When verification is not sufficient or not provided in the online or mail-in redetermination process, send New HEIGHTS-generated AE0055, Proof Needed to Determine Your Assistance . If New HEIGHTS is unavailable, use paper backup BFA Form 808, Proof Needed to Determine Your Assistance .

body:
155.05 Required Verification for Redetermination (AAM)

SR 23-04 Dated 02/23 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

Notify the individual in writing with a verification checklist of any required information or verification needed to complete the redetermination and the due date for returning the verifications.

New HEIGHTS will generate a verification checklist anytime something is entered into the Application Entry screen, and is marked "Not Yet Verified", and eligibility is run.

If New HEIGHTS is unavailable, use the paper backup BFA Form 808, Proof Needed to Determine Your Assistance .

The individual must provide the required verification of all eligibility factors and circumstances requested, no later than 10 working days after the interview.

I f a personal interview is not required, no later than 10 working days after the required return date for DFA Form 771A, Nursing Facility Care Renewal, or BFA Form 800R, Application for Continued Eligibility for Financial, Medical, Child Care, and SNAP Benefits .

Terminate assistance if the individual refuses or fails to provide the required verifications within the time frame.

Exceptions :

• When a third party has not responded to a request for verification within the timeframe, send a follow-up request to the third party and to the individual. Allow an additional 10 working days for a response. If the verification is not provided within the second waiting period, terminate assistance unless the individual provides other acceptable verification.

• If assistance is being terminated due to lack of required verification and the individual provides the required verification within the advance notice period, stop the termination action and reinstate assistance.

Completion of Verification Requirements After the ANP Has Expired

If the assistance was terminated due to lack of verification and the individual provides all the required verification within the 10 days following the end of the advance notice period:

• have the individual fill out BFA Form 800, Application for Assistance , with their name, address, program of assistance, and signature;

• ensure that no other changes have occurred in the case that would affect eligibility and that no new program services have been requested on BFA Form 800 other than those which were originally terminated;

• if the individual meets all program eligibility requirements, reinstate assistance based on the new application date, with no new interview required; and

• generate financial benefits in accordance with PART 119 , BENEFIT DELIVERY TIME FRAMES .

References: He-W 837.01(s), He-W 606.01, He-W 606.100, RSA 167:83,II(c)-(d)

body:
165 EXTENDED MEDICAL ASSISTANCE DUE TO SECTION 1619 STATUS (AAM)

SR 94-04 Dated 04/94 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

Individuals may receive extended medical assistance for an indefinite period, without regard to income, resources, or medical eligibility, if all of the following criteria are met:

. Social Security Administration (SSA) certifies the individual under Section 1619 of the Social Security Act, and

. the individual received medical assistance in the month prior to the month SSA certifies the individual under Section 1619.

SSA determines who is certified under Section 1619 and notifies DFA. The District Office then determines if the individual was receiving medical assistance in the prior month. If the individual was receiving medical assistance in the prior month, the individual remains eligible for extended medical assistance until SSA terminates 1619 status.

165.01 Open Individuals Who Report New or Increased Earnings (AAM)

SR 94-04 Dated 04/94 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

Individuals with SSI benefits who report new or increased earnings may be eligible for extended medical assistance due to Section 1619 status.

1. If the earned income will result in terminating medical assistance eligibility, determine if the individual has advised SSA and if SSA has made a decision about Section 1619 status.

2. If the individual is certified under Section 1619, extend medical assistance indefinitely.

3. If Section 1619 status is pending or the individual has not notified SSA, terminate medical assistance. Advise the individual to reapply for medical assistance if Section 1619 status is received.

body:
165.03 Individuals Who Request Assistance Due to Section 1619 Status (AAM)

SR 94-04 Dated 04/94 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

Individuals who are certified by SSA under Section 1619 and are not receiving medical assistance at the time of certification must complete Form 800, Application , to request medical assistance.

1. Verify if SSA certified the individual under Section 1619.

2. Determine if the individual was receiving medical assistance in the month prior to Section 1619 certification.

3 If the individual was receiving medical assistance in the month prior to Section 1619 certification, a new eligibility determination is not needed. Begin medical assistance as of the first of the month the individual was certified under Section 1619.

4. If the individual was not receiving medical assistance in the month prior to Section 1619 certification, determine eligibility for three-month retroactive medical assistance.

- If the individual was eligible for retroactive medical assistance in the month prior to Section 1619 certification, begin extended medical assistance as of the first of the month the individual was certified under Section 1619.

- If the individual was not eligible for medical assistance in the month prior to Section 1619 certification, determine if the individual is currently eligible for medical assistance under any of the Division ’ s programs. Do not begin extended medical assistance due to Section 1619 status in this situation.

167.01 COLA Income Deduction (AAM)

SR 98-51 Dated 12/98 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

Individuals who meet all of the above requirements are eligible to receive the appropriate SSA cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) as an income deduction.

Compute a COLA income deduction for each individual in the case who is currently receiving SSA income, whether they are the recipient, an applicant, or non-applicant spouse.

Deduct, from the individual ' s current SSA benefit, all the SSA COLAs received after the most recent termination of financial assistance. The amount of the deduction is the difference between the pre- and post-SSA amounts which result from the annual SSA COLA.

207.01 Verification: ANB (AAM)

SR 15-18 Dated 04/15 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

Verify blindness at the initial eligibility determination and verify the Disability Determination Unit (DDU) approval still exists at subsequent redeterminations.

For ANB financial determinations, send the following form when forwarding the request to DDU:

• DDU Form 901, Report of Eye Examination , completed by a licensed ophthalmologist or optometrist.

Additional verification may include any of the following:

• medical records, provided they are no older than 2 years;

• any additional material which may bear on the decision; or

• supplemental information requested by DDU, such as additional evaluations, consultations, or second opinions.

Note: A completed BFA Form 770, Reimbursement Agreement and Acknowledgment , (including all required signatures, dates, and notarized) must be received prior to financial assistance being approved.

References : He-W 601.01; He-W 642.04; RSA 167:6,IV; RSA 167:28

209 AID TO THE PERMANENTLY AND TOTALLY DISABLED (AAM)

SR 26-01 Dated 01/26 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

To be eligible for financial assistance under the Aid to the Permanently and Totally Disabled (APTD) program, an individual must meet all eligibility requirements including:

• ages of 18 through 64;

• meet the requirements in PART 300 , NON-FINANCIAL CRITERIA ;

• meet the financial requirements listed below;

• determined by the Disability Determination Unit (DDU) to be physically or mentally disabled to the extent the individual cannot engage in a substantial gainful employment activity; and

• have a disability that is a condition of physical or mental disease, impairment, or limitation which is likely to result in death, or can be expected to last for a continuous period of not less than 48 months.

The Human Services Specialist (HSS) is responsible for determining if an individual meets the Substantial Gainful Activity (SGA) criteria. SGA applies to initial eligibility only. Individuals with earned income who are applying for APTD must have adjusted earned income, computed by subtracting allowable Impairment Related Work Expenses (IRWE) from gross earned income, of less than $1,690. If the net income exceeds $1,690, the application must be denied.

See the Adult Assistance Manual (AAM) Section 603.01 , Earned Income Disregard , for policy regarding IRWE’s.

References : He-W 601.01; He-W 606.69; He-W 642.03; RSA 167:3-j; 20 CFR 404.1574(b); 20 CFR 404.1575(c); 20 CFR 404.1584(d); 20 CFR 416.974(b); 20 CFR 416.975(c); 20 CFR 416.976; 20 CFR 416.1112(c)(6)

209.01 Verification: APTD (AAM)

SR 24-24 Dated 09/24 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

Verify disability at the initial eligibility determination and verify the Disability Determination Unit (DDU) approval still exists at redeterminations.

For APTD financial determinations, send the following forms when forwarding the request to DDU:

• DDU Form 177, Non-Medical Evaluation of Disability , completed by the individual or authorized representative;

• DDU Form 915, Medical Evaluation Initial , completed by a licensed physician or doctor of osteopathy, if DDU has provided this form as part of a review ; and

• a separate DDU Form 900, Authorization for Release of Medical Records and Information , for each provider/facility listed on DDU Form 177. As well as a DDU Form 900 for SSA.

Additional verification may include any of the following:

• medical records, provided they are no older than 2 years;

• any additional material which may bear on the decision; or

• supplemental information requested by DDU such as additional evaluations, consultations, or second opinions.

Note: A completed BFA Form 770, Reimbursement Agreement and Acknowledgment , (including all required signatures, dates, and notarized) must be received prior to financial assistance being approved.

References: He-W 601.01; He-W 642.03; RSA 167:6,VI; RSA 167:28, 20 CFR 416.960; 20 CFR 416.962

211 QUALIFIED MEDICARE BENEFICIARY (AAM)

SR 94-04 Dated 04/94 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

The Qualified Medicare Beneficiary (QMB) Program provides limited medical assistance coverage to help certain individuals pay their Medicare Part A (hospital insurance) and Part B (supplemental insurance) premiums, premium penalties for late enrollment, Medicare deductibles, and Medicare coinsurance expenses.

To be eligible for assistance under QMB an individual must be entitled to and enrolled in Medicare Part A insurance as determined by the Social Security Administration (SSA).

QMB medical assistance is determined without regard to eligibility for any other public assistance program.

213 SPECIFIED LOW-INCOME MEDICARE BENEFICIARY AND SLMB135 (AAM)

SR 03-04 Dated 01/03 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

The Specified Low-Income Medicare Beneficiary programs (SLMB SLMB135) provide limited medical assistance coverage to help certain individuals pay their Medicare Part B (supplemental insurance) premium and premium penalties for late enrollment.

SLMB and SLMB135 provide full payment of the Medicare Part B premium to eligible individuals.

*

To be eligible for assistance under SLMB or SLMB135 *, an individual must be entitled to Medicare Part B insurance as determined by the Social Security Administration (SSA).

SLMB medical assistance is determined without regard to eligibility for any other public assistance program.

SLMB135 * medical assistance recipients may not be otherwise eligible for Medicaid, including Medicaid In and Out.

214 Independent Living Arrangement (AAM)

SR 22-24 Dated 08/22 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

“Independent living arrangement” means the form of housing for OAA, ANB and APTD recipients and applicants who do not reside in a residential care facility, a community residence, or a licensed and certified nursing facility.

Examples of independent living include private home, apartment, trailer, shared shelter or room rental.

Verify proof of shelter arrangement. Acceptable verification documents need to be in the individual’s name and include:

· Mortgage payment or statement for the residence;

· Signed lease or rental form;

· Property taxes or property insurance;

· Utility bill (electricity, cooking fuel, heating fuel, water/sewage or trash removal); or

· Signed shared shelter form or statement signed by the individual with whom the adult category applicant or recipient resides verifying their shelter expenses.

References: He-W 670.03; He-W 670.04; RSA 167:3-c,I; RSA 167:7; RSA 167:83,I(a); 20 CFR 416.1131; Section 1612(a)(2)(A) Social Security Act

215 RESIDENTIAL CARE FACILITY (AAM)

SR 00-07 Dated 02/00 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

Residential care facilities (RCF) provide personal and social care to elderly or physically disabled adults 18 years of age and older who cannot live alone but do not need to be institutionalized.

Exception: Residents of RCF who meet the medical requirements for Home and Community-Based Care for the Elderly and Chronically Ill (HCBC-ECI - See Part 221 , HOME AND COMMUNITY-BASED CARE FOR THE ELDERLY AND CHRONICALLY ILL ) may be approved for HCBC-ECI services while residing in an RCF.

Determine eligibility for financial assistance or categorically needy medical assistance using the RCF income limits if all of the following are met:

. the individual meets the categorical requirements for either OAA, ANB, or APTD;

. the individual resides in an RCF;

. the RCF is currently licensed by the State of New Hampshire as a sheltered care facility; and

. the individual is appropriate for placement in an RCF.

Determine eligibility using the appropriate independent living income limits if any of the above conditions are not met.

*

See Part 601, Table A , Income Limits , and 611 , Fluctuating Income for information regarding income limits for RCF and independent living arrangements.

For residents of RCF who are approved for HCBC-ECI services, see Part 601, Table B , Income Limits for HCBC Individuals , for information regarding income eligibility for HCBC-ECI services as categorically or medically needy.

215.01 Residential Care Facility Payment (AAM)

SR 25-40 Dated 01/26 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

If the individual is determined eligible for assistance, financial assistance is paid directly to the recipient. The recipient is responsible for paying the Residential Care Facility (RCF).

The individual and the RCF administrator agree on the rate of payment to the RCF.

The recipient is legally entitled to keep a $93 personal needs allowance from monthly income.

body:
217 COMMUNITY RESIDENCE (AAM)

SR 94-04 Dated 04/94 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

Community residences provide personal and social care to mentally ill and developmentally disabled individuals who cannot live alone but do not need to be institutionalized.

Some community residences are considered an enhanced family care facility (EFC) if the residence is owned and operated by a person or family living in the residence. The EFC host family provides services in a certified family environment.

Individuals are entitled to receive one of the community residence standards of need if all of the following are met:

. individual meets the categorical requirements for either OAA, ANB, or APTD;

. individual resides in a community residence;

. if the residence has:

- more than four beds, it must be licensed and certified by the State of New Hampshire,

- four beds or less, it must be certified by the Division of Developmental Services (DDS), or the Division of Behavioral Health (DBH); and

. DDS area agency case manager establishes that the individual is appropriate for placement in a community residence.

Use the independent living standard of need if any of the following are met:

. the residence is not certified or licensed as a community residence;

. the certification or license has expired or is suspended ; or

. the individual is not appropriate for placement in a community residence.

See Part 601 , Income Limits for information regarding standards of need.

217.01 Community Residence Payment (AAM)

SR 25-40 Dated 01/26 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

If the individual is determined eligible for assistance in a community residence, financial assistance is paid directly to the recipient. The recipient is responsible for paying the community residence.

The individual and the community residence manager agree on the rate of payment to the community residence.

The recipient is legally entitled to keep a $93 personal needs allowance from monthly income.

221 HOME AND COMMUNITY-BASED CARE FOR THE ELDERLY AND CHRONICALLY ILL (HCBC-ECI) (AAM)

SR 05-22 Dated 05/05 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

Home and Community-Based Care for the Elderly and Chronically Ill (HCBC-ECI) offers a variety of home and community-based services that an elderly or chronically ill individual may need in order to prevent institutionalization.

Individuals who meet OAA, ANB, APTD, or MEAD categorical requirements may be eligible to receive community-based services if all of the following are met:

. the individual ' s income and resources are within the categorically or medically needy limits for HCBC-ECI services. See Part 601, Table B , Income Limits for HCBC Individuals ;

. Bureau of Elderly and Adult Services(BEAS) has determined there is medical necessity for the individual to receive nursing facility (NF) level of care;

. the individual ' s needs can be met with community services at the same or lower cost than the Medicaid cost of NF level of care as determined by BEAS;

. the individual is residing in either an independent living arrangement or a residential care facility; and

. the individual or their representative has chosen appropriate community-based care as an alternative to institutional care and a physician has approved the choice.

See Medical Assistance Manual, Item 952, for BEAS procedures in determining medical necessity and cost effectiveness of HCBC-ECI.

223 HOME AND COMMUNITY-BASED CARE FOR THE DEVELOPMENTALLY DISABLED (HCBC-DD) (AAM)

SR 03-04 Dated 01/03 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

Home and Community-Based Care for the Developmentally Disabled (HCBC-DD) offers a variety of community-based services that a developmentally disabled individual may need in order to prevent institutionalization.

Individuals who meet the categorical requirements of any Division of Family Assistance (DFA) financial or medical assistance program may be eligible to receive community-based services if all of the following are met:

. Individual ' s income and resources are within the categorically or medically needy limits. See Part 601 , Income Limits;

. Division of Developmental Services (DDS) area agency establishes that the individual is appropriate for community-based services;

. DDS determines the individual has a medical necessity to receive intermediate care facility for the mentally retarded (ICF-MR) level of care (see the Medical Assistance Manual, Item 955 ); and

. Individual or their representative has chosen appropriate community-based care as an alternative to institutional care.

Exception: QMB, SLMB and SLMB135 * MA only cases are not eligible for HCBC Services.

body:
225.01 Disqualified Individuals (AAM)

SR 23-28 Dated 08/23 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

Certain individuals, including fleeing felons and probation or parole violators, are disqualified for not complying with a program requirement.

These individuals continue to be eligible for SSP medical assistance, as long as all other program requirements are met.

Include the income and resources of the disqualified individual per current policy, with all applicable disregards, deductions, etc., allowed. The "needs" of the disqualified individual are not allowed when determining the SSP financial eligibility and benefit amount.

Example : If the SSP financial household size is 2 (husband and wife), and one of the individuals is disqualified, the SSP financial AG size will be 1. The disqualified individual ’ s income and resources still count in full towards the AG, but the income and resource limits for an AG of 1 will be used to determine SSP financial eligibility and benefit amount.

For more information, see PART 319 , FLEEING FELONS AND PROBATION OR PAROLE VIOLATORS .

References : He-W 652.04; He-W 656.07; RSA 167:3-c; RSA 167:6(X)

227 ASSISTANCE GROUP COMPOSITION FOR OAA, ANB, OR APTD: INDEPENDENT LIVING (AAM)

SR 98-51 Dated 12/98 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

The following individuals must be included in the assistance group:

• individual requesting assistance; and

• individual ’ s spouse if they live together.

*

A needy essential person may be included in the financial assistance group at the option of the individual requesting assistance. A needy essential person cannot be included in the medical assistance group. The needy essential person must meet all of the following requirements:

• lives with the individual requesting assistance;

• does not meet the categorical requirements for OAA, ANB, or APTD; and

• is determined by the individual requesting assistance to be essential to their well-being.

body:
301 RESIDENCY (AAM)

SR 94-04 Dated 04/94 Previous Policy

__________________________________________________________________

Individuals must be current residents of New Hampshire to be eligible for benefits. They do not need to have lived or intend to live in NH for any length of time.

Individuals are not eligible for assistance:

· when they are only temporarily in New Hampshire (e.g., here on vacation or to enter temporarily into a New Hampshire medical facility); or

· if they consider another state "home" ( for example, by maintaining a principal residence, voter registration, or car registration in another state with an intent to return).

Also, see AAM 301.01 Absence from New Hampshire .

References : He-W 601.07; He-W 601.08; He-W 606.10; He-W 606.11; He-W 618.02; RSA 21:6; RSA 167:6, I; RSA 167:6, V; RSA 167:78, XXIV

body:
301.01 Absence from New Hampshire Temporary (AAM)

SR 16-06 Dated 01/16 Previous Policy

__________________________________________________________________

Benefits are not affected by a temporary absence from New Hampshire. A temporary absence is when an individual or assistance group is out of the state but intends to keep New Hampshire as their residency and return to the state as soon as the reason for the absence is complete.

Examples of temporary absence include visiting: vacationing, temporary hospitalization, rehabilitation services, and school attendance.

Evaluate residency status in questionable cases or when an individual has been absent from New Hampshire longer than 30 days without notifying the department.

Examples of questionable residency situations include: recurring out-of-state EBT card transactions, out-of-state home ownership or rental, or use of a PO Box, rural route address, or general delivery address to receive mail.

If residency is questionable, evaluate information in the individual’s case and from outside information received about the household circumstances or call the individual. Things to consider are:

• reason for the absence;

• duration and frequency of absence(s);

• where personal and household possessions are kept;

• where the individual votes or pays resident taxes;

• place of employment;

• future plans; and

• in general, all factors which would establish a place of residency.

NOTE : Any one of above examples by itself is not proof that the individual is not a New Hampshire resident.

A written statement that is dated and signed from the individual is sufficient to document their residency unless there is conflicting evidence. If after evaluation residency remains doubtful, mail New HEIGHTS-generated AE0055, Proof Needed to Determine Your Assistance, (or paper backup BFA Form 808, Proof Needed to Determine Your Assistance, if New HEIGHTS is unavailable) to the client to request verification of residency. Enter an expected change in New HEIGHTS to check for verification in 10 days. If the individual does not respond within 10 days or provides insufficient information, deny or close the case.

Example : An FSS receives information that Stuart, who is receiving APTD financial assistance, owns a house in Florida despite his claiming New Hampshire residency. This prompts the FSS to assess other factors. The FSS calls Stuart, but Stuart does not answer. The FSS immediately mails Stuart the New HEIGHTS-generated AE0055, Proof Needed to Determine Your Assistance, to request verification of residency. Stuart submits proof that he does own a house in Florida, and this house is an excluded resource. He also submits proof from his landlord in New Hampshire verifying that he lives in his rental apartment for 10 months out of the year and returns to New Hampshire after his out-of-state visits. The FSS determines that, based on this information, Stuart’s New Hampshire residency is not questionable. The FSS reminds Stuart to notify DHHS anytime he plans to leave New Hampshire for more than 30 days.

For individuals who move out of New Hampshire permanently, financial assistance is to be closed immediately with no ANP.

References: He-W 601.06; He-W 601.07; He-W 601.08; He-W 606.10; He-W 606.11; He-W 618.02; He-W 699.02; RSA 21:6; RSA 167:6, I; RSA 167:6, V; RSA 167:78, XXIV; 42 CFR 435.403

301.03 Out-of-State Recipient Moves into New Hampshire (AAM)

SR 94-04 Dated 04/94 Previous Policy

__________________________________________________________________

When an individual has received benefits in another state prior to applying in New Hampshire, termination of benefits in the prior state of residency must be verified before establishing eligibility for New Hampshire benefits.

The prior out-of-state agency shall be contacted on behalf of all individuals in the household, if the household is unable to provide a proof that benefits have ended or are closing.

305.03 Definition of U.S. Citizen (AAM)

SR 01-17 Dated 06/01 Previous Policy

__________________________________________________________________

U.S. citizens are:

• individuals born in the United States, Puerto Rico, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands, Virgin Islands, American Samoa, or Swain's Island;

• foreign-born children, under age 18, residing in the U.S. with their birth or adoptive parents, at least one of whom is a U.S. citizen by birth or naturalization; and

• individuals granted citizenship status by United States Citizenship Immigration and Naturalization Services (USCIS).

To receive benefits, an individual must be either a U.S. citizen or an eligible qualified alien (see Section 305.07 , Determining Qualified Alien Status ).

References : He-W 601.02; He-W 606.02; 45 CFR 233.50; 42 USC 1320b-7(d)

305.05 Verification of Citizenship and Identity (AAM)

SR 15-07 Dated 01/14 Previous Policy

__________________________________________________________________

Verify citizenship and identity of each assistance group (AG) member at the initial determination of eligibility. For noncitizens, also verify citizenship status at each redetermination.

For most individuals, citizenship and identity are verified via an electronic data crossmatch process through the Social Security Administration (SSA), which uses the individual’s SSN, name, and date of birth to verify citizenship and identity information.

• If the SSA crossmatch fails to verify citizenship and identity, or the individual is unable or is not required to provide a SSN, other acceptable documentary proof of citizenship and identity must be provided.

The documents detailed in the chart below are considered the only acceptable forms of proof for citizenship and identity when applying for most categories of financial assistance.

NOTE: Also see the list of individuals who are exempt from these requirements below.

Citizenship and identity documents that are photocopied, faxed, scanned or copied in another manner (photograph) are considered valid proofs, unless the information on the copied document is inconsistent with other available information or the validity of the copy is questionable. The copied document does not have to be notarized.

PROOFS THAT VERIFY BOTH CITIZENSHIP and IDENTITY NO OTHER PROOF IS NEEDED TO VERIFY CITIZENSHIP AND/OR IDENTITY IF ONE OF THE DOCUMENTS IN THIS TOP SECTION IS SUBMITTED US Passport or US Passport Card (valid or expired if it was issued without limitation) Certificate of Naturalization Certificate of US Citizenship “Enhanced” State Driver’s License (From a state that verifies US Citizenship before issuing the license. License must say “Enhanced Driver License”) Documents issued by a federally recognized Indian Tribe Verification of Citizenship via a Federal or Another State Agency (If done after 7/1/06)

OR

To verify CITIZENSHIP , an individual can submit: 1 Citizenship Document from Column A along with 1 Identity Document from Column B .

COLUMN A CITIZENSHIP DOCUMENTS COLUMN B IDENTITY DOCUMENTS • US Birth Certificate from one of the 50 states and DC; or PR, Guam, USVI, American Samoa, Swain’s Island, or CNMI (some date restrictions apply) • Certification of Report of Birth of US Citizen • Report of Birth Abroad of US Citizen • Certification of Birth • Birth Record Documented by Cross-Match with State Vital Statistics • US Citizen ID Card • Picture Driver’s License (issued only by US state or territory) • Picture School ID • US Military or Draft Card • State, Federal, or local government ID Card • Certificate of Degree of Indian Blood or Tribal Document with Picture • Military Dependent ID Card • US Coast Guard Merchant Marine Card • Northern Marianas ID Card (birth prior to 11/4/86) • Evidence of US Civil Service Employment (if employed prior to 6/1/76) • Final Adoption Decree (With child’s name and US birthplace, if the adoption is not final, a statement from a state approved adoption agency showing the child’s name and US birthplace.) • US Military Record (showing US birthplace) • Data Verification with SAVE Program (or other Dept. of Homeland Security verification process) • Proof of a child meeting the requirements in Section 101 of the Child Citizenship Act of 2000 • Hospital, clinic, doctor, nursing facility, skilled care facility or other medical institution records showing US birthplace. • Life, health, or other insurance records indicating a US place of birth. • Voter’s Registration Card • Proof of Identity Verified by a Federal or State Gov’t. Agency, such as: A Public Assistance, Law Enforcement, Internal Revenue, Tax Bureau, or Corrections Agency • 2 or more documents together , having the individual’s name, and consistent identifying information, such as: - Employer ID Cards - High School/HS Equivalency or College diplomas - Marriage Certificates - Divorce Decrees - Property Deeds/Titles • Official religious documents, recorded in the US, showing a US birthplace • Pre-school, school, Head Start or daycare records with child’s name and US birthplace • Federal or state census record showing US citizenship or US birthplace Special Identity Rules for Children Aged 19 and Younger: Clinic, doctor, hospital or school records, including nursery/daycare records or report cards. If citizenship documents listed above are not available, the individual can submit an affidavit to prove citizenship. It must be signed, under penalty of perjury, by another person who can attest to the individual’s citizenship. The affidavit must contain the individual’s name, date of birth, and US place of birth. It does not have to be notarized. If the above identity documents are unavailable, an individual can submit an affidavit, signed under penalty of perjury, by another person who can attest to the individual’s identity. The affidavit must contain the individual’s name and other identifying information, such as age, sex, race, height, weight, eye color or address. It does not have to be notarized. Individuals must be assisted in obtaining acceptable documentary evidence of citizenship, if assistance is needed.

Exceptions to the Above Citizenship & Identity Requirements:

The following individuals are exempt from the more restrictive identity and citizenship requirements described above:

· individuals who are entitled to or enrolled in Medicare (Part A, Part B, or Part D, for example);

· individuals who receive SSI, verified via the SDX;

· individuals who receive SSDI;

· newborn infants born to women who are current Medicaid recipients. Consider newborns who meet this criteria to have met citizenship and identity requirements at birth. No further proof is needed at subsequent redeterminations. This group includes children whose births were covered by Emergency Medicaid for Non-Citizens; and

· children receiving either Title IV-B services or Title IV-E adoption or foster care payments.

These exempted individuals can verify:

· citizenship with acceptable forms of proof such as birth or hospital records, voter registration cards, U.S. passport, and INS documentation which certifies citizenship or naturalization; and

· identity using any document that reasonably establishes the individual’s identity. If no document is available, use a collateral contact.

If an individual refuses or fails to verify citizenship and/or identity, deny or terminate financial assistance for the entire AG.

Exception: If applicants for financial assistance meet all other program eligibility requirements and the inability to verify citizenship and/or identity is the only reason that prevents a determination of eligibility for the applicant household because:

· the SSA data crossmatch failed to verify the applicant’s citizenship and/or identity; or

· the applicant is unable to provide citizenship and/or identity documentation; or

· the applicant is unable or not required to provide a SSN …

… do not automatically deny assistance. Instead, allow the applicant 95 days from the date on the notice of decision (NOD) to provide the required citizenship and/or identity documentation.

· For applicants who are able to use the SSA data crossmatch, the NOD is the New HEIGHTS-generated DX0011, Citizenship Verification Request .

· For applicants who are not able to use the SSA data crossmatch, the NOD is the generic open notice for financial or medical assistance.

If the required documentation is not provided within 95 days from the date on the NOD, terminate financial assistance for the entire AG.

References : He-W 601.02; He-W 606.02, He-W 606.28, 42 CFR 435.406-407, 45 CFR 233.50, 8 USC 1611-1613

305.09 Eligibility for Certain Qualified Aliens (AAM)

SR 01-24 Dated 08/01 Previous Policy

__________________________________________________________________

Qualified aliens may be eligible for benefits on either an unrestricted or a time-limited basis, depending on type of qualified alien status, or date of entry into the U.S.

Unless specifically mentioned in Section 305.11 , Qualified Aliens Eligible Without Restriction , or 305.13 , Qualified Aliens with Restricted Eligibility Based on Date of Entry into the U.S. , consider the alien to be ineligible.

Exceptions:

· Victims of Trafficking : Non-citizens who have been certified as a victim of trafficking by the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR), and who do not meet the definition of qualified alien, may still be eligible if the individuals were admitted to the U.S. as refugees . See Section 305.11 , Qualified Aliens Eligible Without Restriction , for a description of the eligibility status of refugees. Certified victims of trafficking must meet all other eligibility criteria for a program of assistance in order to receive benefits.

· Native Americans : Native Americans who are members of an Indian tribe as defined in section 4(e) of the Indian Self-determination and Education Assistance Act [25 USC 450(e)], or were born in Canada and are covered under the provisions of section 289 of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 USC 1359) are eligible for financial and/or medical assistance, regardless of qualified alien status. Canadian-born Indians must have at least 50% American Indian blood.

References : He-W 601.01; He-W 601.05; He-W 606.02; He-W 616.02; 8 CFR 1.2; 8 CFR 101.1; 8 CFR 215.1(a); 45 CFR 233.50; 42 USC 1320b-7(d); 8 USC 1158; 8 USC 1255; 8 USC 1611-1613; 8 USC 1641

305.13 Qualified Aliens with Restricted Eligibility Based on Date of Entry into the U.S. (AAM)

SR 97-43 Dated 12/97 Previous Policy

__________________________________________________________________

The following qualified aliens are EITHER :

· Eligible - if residing in the U.S. on or before 8/22/96; OR

· Ineligible - for 5 years from date of entry into the U.S . , when such entry as noted below occurred on or after 8/23/96:

- lawfully admitted permanent residents regardless of work history;

- conditional entrants;

- parolees; and

- victims of battering or extreme cruelty.

All of the above may be eligible after the 5 year period if all other eligibility criteria are met.

305.15 Documentation of USCIS Status (AAM)

SR 04-30 Dated 05/04 Previous Policy

__________________________________________________________________

Require non-citizens to provide United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) documentation of qualified alien status.

Types of USCIS non-citizen documentation include:

· Notifications on USCIS letterhead;

· U.S. stamps on passports; or

· USCIS computer-printed fee receipts.

Non-citizens may also present documentation not issued by USCIS. Verify all non-citizen documentation following the Verification Information System (VIS) verification procedures outlined in Section 305.17 , Verification of Qualified Alien Status .

Exception: If an individual currently receives Social Security, Supplemental Security Income (SSI) or Medicare benefits, and was approved for the same on or after August 22, 1996, this will be accepted as proof of citizenship or qualified alien status.

Non-citizens claiming qualified alien status due to battering or extreme cruelty must provide verification that:

· violence occurred while the individual was residing in the United States;

· the batterer was the spouse or parent of the battered non-citizen, or the non-citizen child’s parent was the subject of the battering;

· the battered spouse or child was residing with the batterer at the time of the incident(s); and

· the battered individual no longer resides with the batterer.

Accept any reasonable evidence of physical violence against the individual, such as:

· police reports;

· information from medical or school personnel;

· photographs; or

· signed statements from individuals familiar with the situation.

References : He-W 601.01; He-W 601.05; He-W 606.02; He-W 616.02; 8 CFR 1.2; 8 CFR 101.1; 8 CFR 215.1(a); 45 CFR 233.50; 42 USC 1320b-7(d); 8 USC 1158; 8 USC 1255; 8 USC 1611-1613; 8 USC 1641

body:
305.17 Verification of Qualified Alien Status (AAM)

SR 04-30 Dated 5/04 Previous Policy

__________________________________________________________________

The United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) maintains various databases on non-citizens in the U.S. Verify the accuracy of documents provided by the non-citizen against USCIS data using the Verification Information System (VIS) primary and secondary verification process.

Primary verification: To initiate primary verification, access VIS through the Internet and follow the instructions on each screen.

Secondary verification: Perform secondary verification procedures when:

· the initial System Response in VIS indicates "Institute Additional Verification"; or

· the information in the VIS Initial Results section does not match the information on the documents provided by the non-citizen.

If requested, provide USCIS with copies of the needed documents and USCIS Form G-845, Verification Request. Attach photocopies of the front and back of all pages of the non-citizen's original documents.

The following chart lists common USCIS documents.

COMMON USCIS DOCUMENTS DOCUMENT DESCRIPTION AND NON-CITIZEN STATUS I-94 - Arrival-Departure Record Issued to most non-citizens upon entry into the U.S. It is attached to an unexpired foreign passport. Often it includes neither an A-number nor a photograph. It also may contain entries such as the following: • Section 203(a)(7)- Conditional Entry • Section 207- Refugee • Section 208- Asylee • Section 212(d)(5)- Parolee • Cuban/Haitian Entrant • Amerasian Immigrant (may have codes AM1, 2, 3 or AM 6, 7, or 8) I-151 (Obsolete) - Alien Registration Receipt Card (Also called "Green Card") Issued to lawful permanent residents prior to June 1978. This form is no longer issued. Although no longer acceptable as verification of lawful permanent resident status, an expired I-151 does not indicate lack of permanent resident status. Encourage the individual to contact BCIS, 1-800-375-5283, for instructions on how to replace the I-151 card with the current I-551 card. I-327 - Reentry Permit Issued to lawful permanent residents (lawful immigrants) before they leave the U.S. for a one- to two-year period. The document bears an expiration date. I-551 - Permanent Resident Card (also called "Green Card" although it is no longer green) Issued to lawful permanent residents after June 1978. Valid indefinitely. Replaced previous Form I-151, which is no longer valid as of 3/20/96. Also known as the "Alien Registration Receipt Card." • Also issued to conditional residents, such as non-citizen spouses of U.S. citizens or lawful residents. When this is the case, the form is only valid until the expiration date on the back. Annotated "CR." I-571 - Refugee Travel Document Issued to non-citizens who have been granted refugee status. This document contains an expiration date. N-560A - Certificate of naturalization Issued for babies verified by USCIS as born to U.S. citizens overseas.

References: He-W 601.01; He-W 601.05; He-W 606.02; He-W 616.02; 8 CFR 1.2; 8 CFR 101.1; 8 CFR 215.1(a); 45 CFR 233.50; 42 USC 1320b-7(d); 8 USC 1158; 8 USC 1255; 8 USC 1611-1613; 8 USC 1641

305.19 When INS Responds Late (AAM)

SR 97-43 Dated 12/97 Previous Policy

__________________________________________________________________

INS should respond to requests for secondary verification within 21 calendar days. If there is no response, call INS to determine the status of the request.

If INS does not respond in a timely manner, base the eligibility decision on the original documents provided by the noncitizen in order to process the case within program time frames. Review the individual's eligibility when secondary verification is received.

References: 8 USC 1373

305.23 Reporting Illegal Aliens to USCIS (AAM)

SR 97-43 Dated 12/97 Previous Policy

__________________________________________________________________

DHHS will notify the following groups within 10 calendar days:

• The United States Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) (attn.: Investigations) whenever a household or assistance group (AG) member proves to be an illegal alien or in any of the following situations:

- Illegally remaining in the U.S.; or

- USCIS documents presented by the household during the application process are determined to be forged;

• The U.S. Attorney General’s office when the alien’s sponsor is sued for failure to provide support and a final civil judgment against the sponsor has been obtained.

Example:

A formal order of deportation or removal presented by the AG during the application or redetermination process is evidence of the USCIS support of the finding of an unlawful presence.

Exception:

Inability or unwillingness to verify noncitizen status is not sufficient for a determination of illegality.

References : He-W 601.01; He-W 606.02; 45 CFR 233.50; 42 USC 1320b-7(d); 8 USC 1644

307.01 Individuals in Designated Receiving Facilities (AAM)

SR 99-09 Dated 03/99 Previous Policy

__________________________________________________________________

Individuals in Designated Receiving Facilities (DRF) may be eligible for adult category financial assistance if they are under the age of 22 or age 65 or older and meet all the eligibility requirements for OAA, APTD, or ANB.

Exception : Eligibility is determined differently depending on the actual or anticipated length of hospitalization.

If the Length of Hospitalization in a Designated Receiving Facility is:

Under 30 Days:

1. Determine eligibility based on the living arrangement that existed prior to hospitalization.

2. Consider the individual temporarily out of the home for medical treatment.

3. Continue financial assistance at the time of hospitalization, as long as the individual remains eligible and there is intent to return home.

30 Days or More:

1. The individual is considered to be residing at the DRF. Financial assistance shall be terminated.

2. If the individual is open for assistance with other group members, terminate assistance for that individual. No Advance Notice Period is required.

References: He-M 405.02; He-W 604.03; He-W 606.18; He-W 624.01; 42 CFR 435.1009 - 435.1010

307.03 Verification (AAM)

SR 94-04 Dated 04/94 Previous Policy

__________________________________________________________________

Contact the institution to verify an individual's residence in an institution, but only when it is a factor of eligibility.

When individuals must reapply for benefits after 30 days, but within 60 days, of admission to a public institution, use the same verification as for reapplications.

When individuals update their eligibility status, verify changes affecting eligibility. Verify within 10 days unless requesting verification directly from a third party, in which case allow an additional 10 days.

Designated Receiving Facilities - The Division of Long Term Supports and Services must provide a signed and dated statement of the anticipated length of hospitalization.

References: He-M 405:02; He-W 601.05; He-W 606.18; He-W 624.01; 42 CFR 435.1009 - 435.1010

309.01 SSN Eligibility and Applicant Notification Requirement (AAM)

SR 98-22 Dated 06/98 Previous Policy

__________________________________________________________________

The law requires that applicants furnish a social security number or verification of an application for a social security number if one has never been issued or the individual cannot provide the number.

Exception : If an applicant cannot provide an SSN or meet the enumeration requirements for a reason beyond their control, good cause may be granted. The District Office Supervisor determines good cause. Approval is limited to a maximum of 1 year, with the initial approval period not to exceed 6 months.

Notify applicants of the above requirements and provide them with Form 758, Notification of Social Security Enumeration Requirement .

309.03 Completing an Application for an SSN (AAM)

SR 98-22 Dated 06/98 Previous Policy

__________________________________________________________________

All applicants who cannot furnish an SSN must apply in person for an original SSN or a replacement SSN card at the U.S. Social Security Administration (SSA).

*

Provide the applicant with an SSA Form SS-5, Application for Social Security Card, and advise the individual to submit Form SS-5 to the nearest SSA office and request Form 5028, Receipt of Application for SSN. Advise the applicant that benefits cannot be issued until verification of enumeration has been submitted or good cause for not enumerating has been determined to exist (See FAM 309.01 , SSN Eligibility and Applicant Notification Requirement ) .

*

Application for an SSN will generate an original social security card. When an original social security card has been lost, application for an SSN will generate a duplicate of the original.

If more than one SSN appears for the same individual, report the duplication to SSA.

If providing the individual with Form SS-5, Application for Social Security Card , complete the NPN block so that SSA can verifiy electronically the issuance of an SSN.

309.05 Verification (AAM)

SR 98-22 Dated 06/98 Previous Policy

__________________________________________________________________

A determination of eligibility may be based on the individual ' s SSN card or SSA Form 5028, Receipt of Application for SSN .

All SSNs furnished by applicants must be verified through an electronic Social Security crossmatch. If the crossmatch does not yield verification, notify applicants that they must provide the information required to verify the SSN or must apply for a replacement SSN card through the nearest SSA office.*

Not meeting SSN requirements results in denial of benefits to the individual for whom there is no SSN. The eligibility and grant amount of the assistance group is computed without consideration of the individual ' s needs.

311 LIABILITY OF RELATIVES TO SUPPORT (AAM)

SR 25-29 Dated 08/25 Previous Policy

__________________________________________________________________

The following relatives are required, if financially able, to contribute to the support of an individual receiving financial assistance.

· spouse; and

Exception: If the couple live together, income and resources of each spouse are considered available to the other when determining eligibility.

· parents (natural or adoptive).

Exception: Parents are only legally liable for children under 18.

Contributions made by relatives are considered unearned income (see Contributions in Part 511 , Income Types .

Liable relatives need to complete and submit BFA Form 64, Legally Responsible Relative Financial Statement . BFA Form 66, Notification of Financial Responsibility will be sent to the relative should they be liable for a monthly contribution.

311.01 Relative's Ability to Contribute (AAM)

SR 26-03 Dated 03/26 Previous Policy

__________________________________________________________________

To evaluate whether a liable relative is able to contribute to the support of an applicant or recipient of financial assistance, consider the following:

• Number of Legal Dependents

The number of legal dependents claimed by the liable relative for IRS purposes

Note: the applicant or recipient is not included as a legal dependent, even if residing with the relative.

• Gross Annual Income

If self-employed, deduct cost of doing business.

• Allowable Deductions

Certain expenses may be deducted from gross annual income before assessing liability or contribution amount. These may include:

o Unreimbursed or unreimbursable medical costs

o Educational expenses

o Court-ordered support or alimony payments

o Repayments, including garnishments, or prior indebtedness

o Business related costs for self-employed individuals

o Exceptional expenses that affect health, safety, or prevent homelessness

Examples include : home repairs, back taxes, transportation for medical services; expenses related to natural disasters such as floods, fires, earthquakes and hurricanes; and expenses resulting from manmade events such as theft of clothing, food or money, eviction, or loss of an owned residence.

Note: All exceptional expenses require written approval from a supervisor.

• Income Threshold Table

The table below is used to assess whether a liable relative has enough income, after allowable deductions, to contribute to the individual.

Legally Liable Relative plus Number of Legal Dependents (excluding the applicant or recipient) Adjusted Gross Annual Income (200% of FPG) (Gross income minus allowable deductions) 1 $31,920 2 $43,280 3 $54,640 4 $66,000 5 $77,360 6 $88,720 7 $100,080 8 $111,440 For each additional dependent add: $11,360

The liable relative’s required contribution is calculated by comparing their gross annual income minus any approved expenses to the amounts listed in the table:

· If their adjusted gross income is less than or equal to the table amount, no contribution is required .

· If their adjusted gross income is greater than the table amount, they must contribute at least 10% of the amount exceeding the table value .

References : He-W 601.05; He-W 622.01(c); RSA 167:3; 42 USC 9902(2)

311.05 Legal Action Against Liable Relatives (AAM)

SR 25-29 Dated 08/25 Previous Policy

__________________________________________________________________

Refer a case to the District Office Supervisor for review when a liable relative is determined able to contribute and they:

· refuse to contribute, or

· refuse to supply adequate information regarding their ability to contribute.

Do not deny or terminate assistance if the legally liable relative fails to cooperate or contribute support. Based on the facts, the BFA Supervisor may refer the case to DHHS's Counsel for Division of Economic Stability. The Counsel determines if a referral to the Attorney General's Office should be made to pursue legal action against the liable relative.

References : He-W 622.01

315.01 Requirements for Developing Potential Sources of Income (AAM)

SR 11-27 Dated 07/11 Previous Policy

__________________________________________________________________

Individuals who are potentially eligible to receive other income or a benefit are required to:

. apply for the other income or benefit, including providing all required information and verification and completing all forms as required in the application process for the other income or benefit;

. cooperate in taking the necessary steps to obtain the other income or benefit;

. accept the other income or benefit, if eligible; and

. pursue all appeal options within the timeframes set by the eligibility-determining agencies or individuals responsible for the other income or benefits, up to, but not including, court action, if found ineligible for the other income or benefit due to medical reasons.

Refer individuals to the appropriate agency to apply for other income or benefits. Individuals must file an application for other income or benefits and verify that they have applied, are cooperating with the application process, and are pursuing all appeal options, if required.

Applicants for OAA, APTD, and ANB financial assistance must apply for all income and benefits for which the applicant is potentially entitled, including SSI and SSA-related benefits, and verify that application has been made, before the financial assistance application can be processed.

*

315.07 Good Cause for Not Developing Potential Sources of Income (AAM)

SR 03-22 Dated 07/03 Previous Policy

__________________________________________________________________

Medical assistance applicants and recipients are exempt from developing potential sources of income if good cause exists. Good cause exists if the individual verifies that a physical, mental, educational, or linguistic limitation prevented the medical assistance applicant or recipient from:

• applying for the other benefits for which they are potentially eligible; or

• taking the necessary steps to obtain the benefits.

If good cause exists, the medical assistance applicant or recipient is exempt from developing potential sources of income until the individual ’ s next redetermination, at which time the exemption must be reviewed and, if good cause continues to exist, the exemption may be extended until the next regularly scheduled redetermination.
